bib.title: On Faithfulness and Factuality in Abstractive Summarization
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2020), pages 1906-1919

question: How often do neural abstractive summarizers hallucinate content unfaithful to the source, how much of it is factual, and can automatic metrics detect it?
hypothesis: Pretrained models hallucinate less and are more faithful/factual, and semantic-inference metrics (entailment) correlate with faithfulness better than ROUGE/BERTScore (implied by the abstract).
contributions: Large-scale human evaluation of intrinsic and extrinsic hallucinations in five XSum systems
Human assessment of whether hallucinated content is factual
Comparison of ROUGE, BERTScore, QA and textual entailment against human faithfulness/factuality
Preliminary use of entailment for model selection

method.summary: Human annotators marked hallucinated spans (intrinsic or extrinsic) and factuality in summaries from four models and the gold references on 500 XSum test articles. Automatic metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore, a BERT-Large MNLI entailment classifier, round-trip-consistency QA) were correlated with the annotations. Entailment was also tried as a selection criterion over four candidate summaries.
method.task: extreme single-sentence abstractive summarization; hallucination evaluation

datasets.name: XSum
datasets.split: train 204,045 (90%), val 11,332 (5%), test 11,334 (5%); 500 random test articles for human evaluation

datasets.name: Multi-NLI
datasets.source: Williams et al. 2018; used to fine-tune the BERT-Large entailment classifier
datasets.preprocessing: sentence-sentence pairs, applied here to document-summary pairs

datasets.name: Natural Questions
datasets.source: Kwiatkowski et al. 2019; used to fine-tune BERT-Base QG, answer extraction and reading comprehension models

models.name: BERTS2S
models.init_from: BERT-Base checkpoints (encoder and decoder); only encoder-decoder attention random

models.name: GPT-TUNED
models.init_from: public GPT-2 checkpoint (Radford et al. 2019), fine-tuned on XSum

other.note: dropped from human study after poor ROUGE

models.name: QA round-trip models
models.architecture: BERT-Base fine-tuned on Natural Questions (QG, answer extraction, reading comprehension; Alberti et al. 2019)

inference.decoding: beam search; beam 10 for PTGEN and TCONVS2S, beam 4 for the Transformer models
inference.samples: one summary per article per system; 500 articles; 3 annotators per item (2500 pairs for hallucination, 1869 for factuality)
inference.retrieval: annotators could use Wikipedia and Google Search for factuality

parameters.entailment model selection: choose among 4 candidate summaries by entailment probability
parameters.ENTAIL->FAITH: entailment model further fine-tuned on faithful annotations (faithful=entailment, else neutral), 5-fold cross-validation; learning rate etc. not stated

other.annotators: trained, fluent English, two pilot studies, pilot documents excluded
other.hallucination criterion: a summary counts as hallucinated if at least one word was marked by all three annotators

metrics.name: Hallucinated I / E / I-union-E
metrics.definition: % of summaries with at least one word annotated by all three annotators as intrinsic/extrinsic hallucination

metrics.name: Faithful+Factual
metrics.definition: faithful summaries plus unfaithful summaries marked factual by all three annotators

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L
metrics.definition: overlap with reference; R1,R2 informativeness, RL fluency

metrics.name: Textual entailment
metrics.definition: BERT-Large MNLI entailment probability between document and summary; entail/neutral/contradict shares

metrics.name: QA
metrics.definition: % of questions generated from summary that are answered correctly from the document

metrics.name: Spearman |rs|
metrics.definition: correlation of metric with faithful and factual human labels

eval.protocol: One-way ANOVA with post-hoc Tukey HSD, p<0.01, for pairwise system comparisons; Fleiss kappa for agreement; 5-fold CV for ENTAIL->FAITH.

results.claim: BERTS2S leads on ROUGE-1 on the 500-item sample.
GPT-TUNED had the lowest ROUGE-1 and was dropped from the human study.
Textual entailment correlates best with faithfulness (moderate).
Entailment correlation with factuality is weak.
ROUGE-1 correlates very weakly with faithfulness.
QA-based score correlates almost not at all with faithfulness.
Selecting among four systems' outputs by entailment raises faithfulness by almost 5 points absolute, costing ROUGE.
Fine-tuning the entailment model on faithful annotations gives a small further gain with better ROUGE.
BERTS2S gold-contradiction rate in entailment is lowest among systems, at par with GOLD.
Annotator agreement on hallucination is substantial.

limits: Only XSum, whose gold summaries are introductory sentences with many extrinsic additions, so gold counts as unfaithful.
Only 500 test articles and five systems from 2017-2020; no models larger than BERT-Base/GPT-2-small scale.
Entailment is reference-less and can be gamed (first sentence is always entailed), so must be paired with ROUGE.
Entailment classifier trained on sentence pairs, not document-summary pairs; QA metric correlated very weakly, authors blame error compounding.
ENTAIL->FAITH trained on small annotation set (5-fold CV); authors expect larger gains with more data.
Does not propose a solution to hallucination.
